newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia bonds look to RBA to enliven drab market.
newsitem.headline: Australia bonds look to RBA to enliven drab market.

text.p: *Australian bonds turned narrowly mixed during a slow morning hoping that the Reserve Bank quarterly bulletin may breath some life into the market.
Australian bonds turned narrowly mixed during a slow morning hoping that the Reserve Bank quarterly bulletin may breath some life into the market.

Yields had eased slightly initially on the back of a firm U.S. Treasury market, but what interest there was largely concentrated on futures, where contracts remained contained to their recent ranges, traders said.
"The market is holding out for the bulletin. But to be honest I can't see it differing much from (governor) MacFarlane's speech last week, so sadly it could be a non-event," said one trader.

A less hawkish than expected speech by Macfarlane, combined with a benign final reading for second wages growth last week, has stirred up thoughts of a policy easing, although bill futures are in need of a bit more stimulus to maintain their deep discounts to current 5.0 percent official rates.
December bills were slightly softer at 95.23, but still equate to a cash rate of 4.77 percent.

U.S. yields hardened slightly in Tokyo trading, which took the edge off the local market's early firm tone. The U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meets later on Tuesday, but no change in monetary policy is expected.

The local market showed a mild outperforming bias against the U.S., reversing some of the spread widening seen late on Monday. New Zealand debt was once again under pressure as the fragility of the N.Z. dollar continued to weigh on the market.
